name: Fluticasone propionate
route_note: Inhaled twice daily for asthma/COPD; nasal spray once daily; cream or ointment for skin

discovery.note: A trifluorinated androstane carbothioate designed for high receptor affinity and near-complete first-pass inactivation.

rx_status: prescription; nasal spray OTC in the US and elsewhere
tagline: High-potency inhaled and nasal corticosteroid with very low oral bioavailability
summary: Fluticasone propionate is a potent synthetic glucocorticoid used as an inhaled controller for asthma and COPD, as a nasal spray for allergic rhinitis and topically for inflammatory skin disease. Swallowed drug is almost entirely inactivated in the liver.
mechanism: Fluticasone binds the glucocorticoid receptor with high affinity; the activated receptor suppresses transcription of inflammatory cytokines, chemokines and adhesion molecules and induces anti-inflammatory proteins.

Locally this reduces eosinophilic airway inflammation and mucosal oedema. Oral bioavailability is below 1% because CYP3A4 converts it to an inactive 17β-carboxylic acid, so systemic effects arise mainly from drug absorbed through the lungs.

history.title: Discovery
history.detail: Fluticasone propionate is synthesised at Glaxo.

history.title: First approval
history.detail: Introduced for medical use, initially in the UK.

history.title: Flovent
history.detail: FDA approves Flovent inhalation aerosol for asthma.

history.title: OTC nasal spray
history.detail: FDA approves Flonase Allergy Relief for non-prescription use.

history.title: Generic combination
history.detail: First generic fluticasone/salmeterol inhaler (Wixela Inhub) approved in the US.

pk.bioavailability: Oral <1%; nasal <2%; inhaled roughly 10–30% depending on device

serious: Cushing's syndrome and adrenal suppression with ritonavir or other strong CYP3A4 inhibitors

facts: Co-administration with ritonavir has caused iatrogenic Cushing's syndrome from inhaled or nasal fluticasone.
Fluticasone furoate is a different ester with distinct pharmacology, used in once-daily products.
